design.approach: Worktree-isolated build. P2 first (additive /2 schemas + dual-revision readers across all consumers + evaluator contract + corpus migration + non-disruption guard + evaluator spike), then the four independent loop changes (P3-P6, file-disjoint), serialized regen after each phase (T011/T012), then integration acceptance + docs (P7). Enforcement is an in-loop, per-run, binding evaluator receipt; /1 stays valid via dual-revision readers.
design.authority: csm-orchestrate remains the single coordination entry; no new acceptance authority.

discoveredRequirements.requirement: Worktree isolation for the build: the live skills dir is shared with concurrent agents.
Registry immutability: new /2 ids only; dual-revision readers; serialized same-commit regen.
No shared lock/shared mutable state in the skills dir; enforcement per-run local.
Scope corpus migration to goal-owned tracked files; never sweep foreign artifacts.

constraints: Worktree isolation: execute the whole plan inside a dedicated `wt/csm-completion-fixes` worktree (scripts/wt-session.mjs); `main` stays on the last-good tree until a serial merge at P7. No task edits the live skills dir directly.
Non-disruptive contract: additive-only /2 schemas; /1 frozen and still read by every consumer; no breaking change to existing artifacts or in-flight runs.
Enforcement lives inside each skill's loop — not in the Makefile or CI.
No new global lock or shared mutable state in the skills directory; enforcement state is per-run local so concurrent invocations are never serialized.

Shared generated artifacts (bootstrap/package/**, bootstrap/payload-index.json, csm-orchestrate/capabilities.json) are regenerated ONLY by the serialized tasks T011/T012, so parallel groups never race pack-bootstrap's fail-fast lock.
Registry immutability: never edit /1 schemas; /2 ids only; dual-revision readers; same-commit regen via T011/T012.
Never stage, sweep, or delete a path this goal did not create (foreign/uncommitted artifacts are out of scope).
